Subject: Recap: Reliability hypotheses from today’s discovery + proposed next steps

Hi Priya / Marco —

Thanks again for the time today. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, our initial hypotheses around reliability/graceful degradation, and a set of recommended next steps so we can move toward a scoped pilot. Please correct anything I got wrong.

Key pain points you described
- Intermittent tokenization timeouts on peak batch windows (monthly payroll runs and end-of-day reconciliations).
- Lack of predictable degraded-mode behavior: currently requests either succeed or time out; there’s no soft-fail fallback.
- Regulatory requirement to pin processing to specific regions during certain workflows (data residency constraints).

Current stack (as mentioned)
- Primary inference: on-prem GPUs (NVIDIA A100), managed by internal orchestration (Kubernetes + custom autoscaler).
- Fallback: currently none (manual operator intervention).
- Observability: ELK stack for logs, Datadog for metrics, manual post-incident RCA.

Success criteria you shared
- 99.95% availability for core reconciliation flows during business hours (SLO target).
- Max 350ms p99 latency for customer-facing prompts under normal load.
- On degradation, deterministic fallback to a smaller/quantized model or regional reroute with documented QA acceptance.

Our reliability hypotheses (high level)
1) Prefix/KV caching across recurring reconciliation prompts will reduce token compute and reduce p95/p99 latency spikes.
2) Pre-defined fallback model families (quantized 7B -> 3B) + region-aware routing will allow graceful degradation without manual ops.
3) SLO-driven routing (latency-first on critical flows, cost-first on non-critical) can keep core flows within your SLA while lowering unit cost.

What we propose next (short-term pilot scope)
1) Discovery deliverable: a one-page SLO matrix mapping ATB critical flows to fallback strategies and test cases (attached: atlas_slo_hypotheses.xlsx).
2) Workshop (2 hours): Neha + Monica join your infra team to validate network egress constraints and KMS requirements (proposed week of Aug 10).
3) Technical spike (2 weeks): deploy a shadowed endpoint running Redwood Private in your staging region with two fallback model variants + region-aware routing.
4) Definition of success for pilot: measurable p95/p99 improvement or documented graceful degradation behavior during injected load tests.

Attachments included
- atlas_slo_hypotheses.xlsx (initial SLO matrix & test cases)
- fallback-routing-diagram.png (sketch of routing + region failover)
- mutual-action-plan-ATB.docx (template MAP to finalize timeline and owners)

Proposed immediate actions
- Priya / Marco: confirm availability for the workshop week of Aug 10 and the primary technical contact for your infra team.
- Monica / Neha: I’ll leave the technical scheduling details with you once Priya confirms contacts.

If that looks right, I’ll follow up with an updated MAP and calendar invites.

Thanks —

Priya / Marco —

Quick technical note: for the staging spike we recommend a conservative fallback chain: production model (full precision, region-local) -> quantized model in same region -> model in secondary region (quantized) -> synthetic response mode (very small model returning canned responses) — each step must emit a degradation event so your downstream systems can mark the response as degraded.

I’ve attached a one-page checklist and the routing diagram to the MAP draft. Happy to walk through during the workshop.
